data.name: Plugin.Name
data.value: Libre Hardware Monitor

data.name: Plugin.Description
data.value: Reads hardware sensors and exposes them as Macro Deck variables.

data.name: Configuration.Title
data.value: Libre Hardware Monitor

data.name: Configuration.Description
data.value: The sensor window opens in your browser: the Macro Deck 2 dialog, with the whole tree of hardware, reading kind and sensor, the polling rate under it, and a checkbox that asks Windows for administrator rights at every start. Press Continue to open it, and tick the sensors to publish as Macro Deck variables there - what you tick is what is saved. Sensors you leave out stay available from the variable catalog, and the names the Macro Deck 2 plugin used are kept, so an upgraded button keeps working.

data.name: Configuration.UnknownStep
data.value: Unknown step.

data.name: Configuration.WindowRefused
data.value: The sensor window could not be opened in a browser. Press Continue to try again.

data.name: Configuration.WindowLost
data.value: The sensor window closed without sending its selection back. Press Continue to open it again.

data.name: Issues.ReadingsMissing.Title
data.value: Some readings are missing

data.name: Issues.ReadingsMissing.Action
data.value: Open the sensor window

data.name: Issues.ReadingsMissing.EnableAction
data.value: Enable elevated readings

data.name: Issues.ReadingsMissing.Resolved
data.value: Opening the sensor window.

data.name: Issues.ReadingsMissing.Elevated
data.value: Elevated readings are on. To have them at every start, tick Start elevated readings at startup in the plugin's settings.

data.name: Issues.ReadingsMissing.ElevationCancelled

data.name: Issues.ReadingsMissing.ElevationFailed

data.name: Issues.ReadingsMissing.Unknown

data.name: Actions.Sensor.Label
data.value: Fan

data.name: Actions.Sensor.Description
data.value: The fan or pump to control.

data.name: Actions.NoControls
data.value: No controllable fans or pumps were found on this machine.

data.name: Actions.NoControlsBlocked
data.value: No controllable fans or pumps were found. The hardware library's driver is not available to this process, which is what hides them; use Enable elevated readings in Macro Deck's issue list, or start Macro Deck as an administrator, to make them appear.

data.name: Actions.ControlsUnavailable
data.value: The controllable fans or pumps could not be read. The hardware library reported an error.

data.name: Actions.NoSensorSelected
data.value: Pick a fan first.

data.name: Actions.SensorGone
data.value: That fan is no longer present. Pick it again.

data.name: Actions.ControlFailed
data.value: The fan did not accept the change. The hardware library reported an error.

data.name: Actions.SetFanSpeed.Name
data.value: Set fan speed

data.name: Actions.SetFanSpeed.Description
data.value: Sets a controllable fan or pump to a percentage of its range. The hardware library's driver must be loaded, which needs the elevated hardware helper or Macro Deck running as administrator.

data.name: Actions.SetFanSpeed.Percent.Label
data.value: Speed

data.name: Actions.SetFanSpeed.Percent.Description
data.value: Percentage of the fan's own range. 0 is as slow as the chip allows; 100 is full speed.

data.name: Actions.SetFanSpeed.InvalidPercent
data.value: The speed is missing or not a number.

data.name: Actions.RestoreFanControl.Name
data.value: Restore fan control

data.name: Actions.RestoreFanControl.Description
data.value: Hands a fan or pump back to the motherboard's own fan curve, undoing a speed set by software.

data.name: Variables.Write.InvalidValue
data.value: The value is missing or not a number.

data.name: Variables.Write.NotFound
data.value: That sensor is no longer known to the plugin.

data.name: Variables.Write.Unavailable
data.value: The sensor cannot be controlled right now. Fan control needs the elevated hardware helper, or Macro Deck running as administrator, with the hardware driver loaded.
